title: Fundamental Objectives & Directive Principles (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: Chapter II sets broad state policy goals (political, economic, social, environmental). Many provisions are not directly enforceable in court as individual rights but guide interpretation and legislation—contrast with fundamental rights in Chapter IV.

title: Fundamental Rights (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: Chapter IV protects rights such as life, dignity, personal liberty, fair hearing, privacy, thought, expression, assembly, and freedom from discrimination in prescribed circumstances. Limitation clauses and derogations during emergencies matter in practice.

title: Federal structure — federal vs state powers (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: Nigeria’s Constitution divides legislative powers among the federal government, states, and (where provided) local government areas. Exclusive and concurrent lists determine who can legislate on topics like security, commerce, and land.

title: Judicature & Supreme Court (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: the Constitution establishes the judiciary, culminating in the Supreme Court as final appellate authority on many matters, with powers of interpretation that can invalidate inconsistent laws or conduct.
